original_record.title: Chepoi–Estellon–Vaxès linear Erdős–Pósa conjecture for planar ball hypergraphs
original_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph and let $
u_{\ell}(G)$ and $\tau_{\ell}(G)$ denote, respectively, the packing number and transversality of its hypergraph of balls of radius $\ell$. **Chepoi–Estellon–Vaxès' conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that, for every $\ell$ and every planar graph $G$, 

$$
\tau_{\ell}(G) \leq c \cdot \nu_{\ell}(G).
$$

This conjecture asks for a linear gap between the packing and transversal numbers. It is subsumed by the stated result of Dvořák for bounded-expansion classes only with a coefficient depending on $\ell$, so the planar linear bound remains unresolved in the supplied text.
original_record.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet and Stéphan Thomassé, “VC-dimension and Erdős-Pósa property”, arXiv:1412.1793 (2014).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1793

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2014).

original_record.title: Hamiltonian cycle interval conjecture for generalized polygons
original_record.statement:
Let $s\ge 2$ and $n\ge 3$, and let $\mathcal{G}=({{\mathcal P}},{{\mathcal L}};{\mathcal I})$ be a generalized $n$-gon of order $s$, so its Levi graph is $(s+1)$-regular, has diameter $n$, and has girth $2n$. Write

$$
p_s^{(n)}=s^{n-1}+s^{n-2}+\cdots+s+1.
$$

Here $C_k$ denotes a cycle of length $k$, and $C_k\hookrightarrow\mathcal{G}$ means that $C_k$ embeds in the Levi graph of $\mathcal{G}$. **Hamiltonian cycle interval conjecture.** Then $C_k\hookrightarrow\mathcal{G}$ for all integers $k$ satisfying

$$
n\le k\le p_s^{(n)}.
$$

Generalized $n$-gons are finite partial planes whose Levi graphs have the specified regularity, diameter, and girth; the conjecture extends the paper's cycle-embedding result for projective planes. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
original_record.source_name: Felix Lazebnik, Keith E. Mellinger and Oscar Vega, “Embedding cycles in finite planes”, arXiv:1305.2646 (2013).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.2646

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

original_record.title: Chen–Chvátal conjecture for finite metric spaces
original_record.statement:
Let $(V,d)$ be a finite metric space with $n$ points. For distinct points $x,y,z\in V$, say that $z$ lies between $x$ and $y$ when

$$
d(x,y)=d(x,z)+d(z,y).
$$

For distinct $x,y\in V$, define the **line** generated by $x$ and $y$ by

$$
\overline{xy}=\{x,y\}\cup\{z\in V: d(z,y)=d(z,x)+d(x,y)\ \lor\ d(x,y)=d(x,z)+d(z,y)\ \lor\ d(x,z)=d(x,y)+d(y,z)\}.
$$

A metric space has a **universal line** if its whole point set is a line. **Chen–Chvátal conjecture.** Every finite metric space of $n$ points without a universal line determines at least $n$ distinct lines. The conjecture extends the de Bruijn–Erdős theorem from the Euclidean plane to arbitrary finite metric spaces and remains open in general, although it is known for graphs of diameter three.
original_record.source_name: Martín Matamala and Luciano Villarroel-Sepúlveda, “Chen-Chvátal Conjecture for Graphs of Diameter 3”, arXiv:2512.12047 (2025).
original_record.references:
**9 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2511.17156](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17156), [arXiv:2310.15058](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15058), [arXiv:1808.08710](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.08710), [arXiv:1803.07154](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07154), [arXiv:1501.06681](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.06681), [arXiv:1412.8283](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.8283), [arXiv:1402.5627](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.5627), [arXiv:1312.3214](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3214).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12047

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “The Chen--Chvátal conjecture is open even in metric spaces induced by connected graphs.”

original_record.title: Bartnicki–Grytczuk–Niwczyk list 1-2-3 Conjecture
original_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with no component isomorphic to $K_2$. An **edge $k$-list-weighting** assigns to each edge a weight from an independently assigned list of $k$ real numbers. Let $\operatorname{ch}_\Sigma^e(G)$ be the least $k$ such that every assignment of lists of size $k$ to the edges permits an edge list-weighting giving different incident-edge sums to adjacent vertices. **Bartnicki–Grytczuk–Niwczyk's list 1-2-3 Conjecture.** If $G$ is nice, then

$$
\operatorname{ch}_\Sigma^e(G)\leq 3.
$$

This strengthens the ordinary 1-2-3 Conjecture by allowing arbitrary edge lists. The paper states it as a conjecture and develops sequence analogues, so it remains open in the source.
original_record.source_name: Ben Seamone and Brett Stevens, “Sequence variations of the 1-2-3 Conjecture and irregularity strength”, arXiv:1211.0463 (2012).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.0463

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

original_record.title: Sequence list 1-2-3 Conjecture for arbitrary edge orderings
original_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with no component isomorphic to $K_2$. Fix an ordering of $E(G)$. A **sequence edge $k$-list-weighting** assigns to each edge a weight from its independently assigned list of $k$ real numbers; each vertex receives the sequence of weights on its incident edges in the fixed edge order. Let $\operatorname{ch}_\sigma^e(G)$ be the least $k$ such that every edge-list assignment permits a weighting whose vertex sequences distinguish adjacent vertices. **The sequence list 1-2-3 Conjecture.** If $G$ is nice, then

$$
\operatorname{ch}_\sigma^e(G)\leq 3.
$$

This is the sequence analogue of the list 1-2-3 Conjecture for every ordering of the edge set. The paper introduces it as an open conjecture after proving only larger general bounds.
original_record.source_name: Ben Seamone and Brett Stevens, “Sequence variations of the 1-2-3 Conjecture and irregularity strength”, arXiv:1211.0463 (2012).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.0463

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

original_record.title: Aharoni–Berger–Raisman's hypergraph matching conjecture
original_record.statement:
Let $H$ be a 3-partite 3-uniform hypergraph with partition classes $V_1,V_2,V_3$ satisfying

$$
|V_2|=|V_3|=|V_1|+1.
$$

For every $x\in V_1$, the hyperedges containing $x$ induce a perfect matching of $V_2\cup V_3$. **Aharoni–Berger–Raisman's matching conjecture.** The vertex class $V_1$ is matchable, meaning that $H$ has a matching containing all vertices of $V_1$. This conjecture is presented as equivalent to the one-vertex-per-part special case of the distortion-colouring problem and as a strengthening of the Brualdi–Stein conjecture; its general status is open.
original_record.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos, “Delay colourings of cubic graphs”, arXiv:1211.1306 (2013).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.1306

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

original_record.title: Frank's vertex-connected orientation conjecture
original_record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph and let $k$ be a positive integer. A **$k$-vertex-connected orientation** is an orientation of $G$ that is $k$-vertex-connected. **Frank's conjecture.** $G$ has a $k$-vertex-connected orientation if and only if $|V|\geq k+1$ and $G-X$ is $2(k-|X|)$-edge-connected for all $X\subseteq V$ with $|X|\leq k-1$.

The conjecture was proved for $k=2$ by Thomassen, but was disproved for every $k\geq 3$ by Durand de Gevigney; deciding whether a graph has a $k$-vertex-connected orientation is NP-hard for every $k\geq 3$.
original_record.source_name: Florian Hörsch and Zoltán Szigeti, “A note on 2-vertex-connected orientations”, arXiv:2112.07539 (2021).
original_record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1212.4086](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4086), [arXiv:1201.3727](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.3727).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07539

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

original_record.title: Thomassen's conjecture on good vertex pairs in arc-strong digraphs
original_record.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. It is **$k$-arc-strong** if $D\setminus A^{\prime}$ remains strong for every subset $A^{\prime}\subseteq A(D)$ of size at most $k-1$. An **out-branching** of $D$ is a spanning oriented tree in which every vertex except its root has in-degree one, and an **in-branching** is a spanning oriented tree in which every vertex except its root has out-degree one. A **good $(u,v)$-pair** is a pair of arc-disjoint out-branching and in-branching rooted at $u$ and $v$, respectively.

**Thomassen's conjecture.** There exists an integer $K$ such that every $K$-arc-strong digraph $D=(V,A)$ has a good $(u,v)$-pair for every choice of $u,v\in V$.

This conjecture asks for a uniform arc-connectivity condition guaranteeing compatible branchings with arbitrary prescribed roots. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
original_record.source_name: Jiangdong Ai, Yiming Hao, Zhaoxiang Li and Qi Shao, “Arc-disjoint in- and out-branchings in semicomplete split digraphs”, arXiv:2410.12575 (2024).
original_record.references:
**7 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2309.06904](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06904), [arXiv:2302.08283](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.08283), [arXiv:2302.06177](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06177), [arXiv:2206.12092](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12092), [arXiv:2012.03742](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03742), [arXiv:2007.02834](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.02834).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12575

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

original_record.title: Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture for dense linear triple systems
original_record.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$ and $0<\delta\leq 1$. A **linear $3$-graph** is a $3$-uniform hypergraph in which any two edges share at most one vertex; for a linear $3$-graph $\mathcal{H}$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, its linear density is

$$
d^{\operatorname{lin}}(\mathcal{H})=\frac{3m}{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

A $(k+3,k)$-configuration is a set of $k$ edges whose union contains at most $k+3$ vertices. **Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture for dense linear triple systems.** For every $k\geq 4$ and $0<\delta\leq 1$ there exists $n_0=n_0(k,\delta)$ such that every linear $3$-graph $\mathcal{H}$ with $n\geq n_0$ vertices and $d^{\operatorname{lin}}(\mathcal{H})\geq\delta$ contains a $(k+3,k)$-configuration. The general Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture is known in the case $k=3$ by the Ruzsa–Szemerédi $(6,3)$-theorem, while the cases $k\geq 4$ remain open; the paper proves the assertion for densities $\delta>4/5$.
original_record.source_name: Giovanne Santos and Mykhaylo Tyomkyn, “The Brown-Erdős-Sós conjecture in dense triple systems”, arXiv:2508.09841 (2025).
original_record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2011.13678](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13678).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.09841

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2025).

original_record.title: Graceful difference labeling conjecture for disjoint unions of circuits
original_record.statement:
Let $G=(V,A)$ be a directed graph. A **graceful difference labeling** (gdl) of $G$ is a bijection

$$
f:V\rightarrow\{1,\ldots,|V|\}
$$

such that the labels $f(v)-f(u)$ assigned to the arcs $uv\in A$ are distinct. For $k\geq 2$, let $\overrightarrow{\mathbf C_k}$ denote the directed circuit on $k$ vertices, and let a disjoint union of circuits be a graph formed by taking disjoint unions of such directed circuits.

**Graceful difference labeling conjecture.** If $G$ is the disjoint union of circuits, then $G$ has a gdl, unless

$$
G=\overrightarrow{\mathbf C_3}\quad\text{or}\quad G=\overrightarrow{\mathbf C_2}+\overrightarrow{\mathbf C_3}.
$$

The conjecture extends the cases established in the paper, including the fact that $n\overrightarrow{\mathbf C_3}$ has a gdl if and only if $n\geq 2$. The two displayed graphs are known exceptions; the general assertion for all disjoint unions of circuits remains open.
original_record.source_name: Alain Hertz and Christophe Picouleau, “On graceful difference labelings of disjoint unions of circuits”, arXiv:1908.11300 (2019).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11300

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

original_record.title: Shifted Chvátal-resilience conjecture for Hamilton cycles in random graphs
original_record.statement:
Let $G=G_{n,p}$ be a random graph, and let $(\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},\boldsymbol{\delta})$-Chvátal-resilience mean resilience with respect to subgraphs satisfying the shifted Chvátal degree condition: there is an ordering $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ with $d_H(v_1)\geq\cdots\geq d_H(v_n)$ such that, for every $i<n/2$, either

$$
d_H(v_i)\leq (n-i)p-\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}np
$$

or

$$
d_H(v_{n-i-\boldsymbol{\delta} n})\leq ip-\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}np.
$$

**Shifted Chvátal-resilience conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $C>0$ such that, for $p\geq C\log n/n$, a.a.s. the random graph $G_{n,p}$ is $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$-Chvátal-resilient with respect to Hamiltonicity.

This conjecture proposes the Hamilton-cycle analogue of the preceding theorem for perfect matchings, extending Chvátal-type resilience to Hamiltonicity in sparse random graphs. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

original_record.title: LOCC hierarchy conjecture for multipartite entanglement classes
original_record.statement:
Let $P_\text{III}$ be the poset of nonempty up-sets labeling the classes, and let $\mathcal{C}_{\underline{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}}$ denote the class with label $\underline{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}$. Write $\mathcal{C}_{\underline{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}\overset{\operatorname{LOCC}_\mathrm{s}}{\longrightarrow}\mathcal{C}_{\underline{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}}$ for conversion by the specified LOCC relation, and let $P_{\text{III},\mathcal{C}}$ be the set of these classes.

**LOCC hierarchy conjecture.** For all $\underline{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},\underline{\boldsymbol{\beta}}\in P_\text{III}$,

$$
\mathcal{C}_{\underline{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}\overset{\operatorname{LOCC}_\mathrm{s}}{\longrightarrow}\mathcal{C}_{\underline{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\underline{\boldsymbol{\beta}}\preceq\underline{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},
$$

so that

$$
(P_{\text{III},\mathcal{C}},\geq_\mathrm{s})\cong(P_\text{III},\preceq).
$$

The claim would identify the LOCC convertibility hierarchy with the combinatorial hierarchy of class labels, turning the known one-way implication into an exact characterization. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.

original_record.title: Exchange-graph isomorphism and seed-exchange-matrix reconstruction conjecture
original_record.statement:
Let $d4d0$ and $d4d0'$ be connected cluster algebras, each of finite type or skew-symmetric finite mutation type. Let $d4e2=(\mathbf{x},B)$ and $d4e2'=(\mathbf{x}',B')$ be seeds of $d4d0$ and $d4d0'$, respectively. For a seed $d4e2$, let $N(\ell^k_{d4e2})$ denote the associated quantity appearing in the source, for $k\in\mathbb{Z}^{*}$. **Exchange-graph and matrix conjecture.** If $N(\ell^k_{d4e2})=N(\ell^k_{d4e2'})$ for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}^{*}$, then there is an isomorphism

$$
\sigma:E_\mathcal{A}\to E_{\mathcal{A}'}
$$

satisfying $d4d7(d4e2)=d4e2'$. Moreover, assuming that neither $d4d0$ nor $d4d0'$ is of rank $2$ or type $F_4$, the same equality implies

$$
B\cong B'\quad\text{or}\quad B\cong -B'.
$$

The claim relates numerical data associated with loops in exchange graphs to their global isomorphism type and, except for the stated rank-$2$ and type-$F_4$ cases, to the exchange matrices of corresponding seeds. The supplied parser marks its resolution status as unknown, so the database records it as open.

original_record.title: Compactified weak convergence for rooted minor-excluding graphs
original_record.statement:
Let $\mathbb G^*$ be the compactification of rooted countable graphs introduced in the paper, with metric $d$. Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite set of finite connected graphs, and let $Ex^{\bullet}(\mathcal S)$ be the class of rooted, labelled or unlabelled, connected graphs with no minor in $\mathcal S$. Let $R_n$ be a uniformly random element of $Ex^{\bullet}(\mathcal S)$ with $n$ vertices.

**Compactified rooted convergence conjecture.** The sequence $R_n$ converges weakly with respect to $d$.

The compactification allows infinite-degree vertices and is compact, so every sequence has a convergent subsequence. The conjecture asserts convergence of the entire sequence for minor-excluding classes; it is closely related to the earlier rooted weak-convergence formulation but is not merely ordinary weak convergence.

original_record.title: The Erdős–Ko–Rado-type conjecture for L-intersecting families
original_record.statement:
Let $0<s\leq k\leq n$ be positive integers. Let $L=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_s\}$ be a set of $s$ positive integers such that $0<\ell_1<\cdots<\ell_s$. Suppose that $n>k^2-k+1$. Let $\mathcal F=\{F_1,\ldots,F_m\}$ be an **$L$-intersecting, $k$-uniform family** of subsets of $[n]$, meaning that $|F_i\cap F_j|\in L$ for every distinct $F_i,F_j\in\mathcal F$. **The Erdős–Ko–Rado-type conjecture for $L$-intersecting families.** Then

$$
m\leq {n-\ell_1\choose s}.
$$

Moreover, if

$$
|\mathcal F|={n-\ell_1\choose s},
$$

then there exists a set $T\in {[n]\choose \ell_1}$ such that $T\subseteq F$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. This conjecture extends the preceding bound and its equality characterization from the proven range to the stated condition $n>k^2-k+1$; the projective-plane example motivating it shows why the threshold is natural. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
original_record.source_name: Gábor Hegedüs, “A generalization of the Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorem”, arXiv:1512.05531 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05531

original_record.title: Bonamy–Kardoš–Kelly–Nelson–Postle conjecture on bounded critical number
original_record.statement:
A **simple binary matroid** is a restriction of a finite binary projective geometry $\operatorname{PG}(n-1,2)$. It is **$I_s$-free** if it has no $s$-element independent flat, and its **critical number** is $n-k$, where $k$ is the dimension of a largest subgeometry of $\operatorname{PG}(n-1,2)$ disjoint from the matroid. A matroid is **triangle-free** if it has no triangle restriction. 

**Bonamy–Kardoš–Kelly–Nelson–Postle conjecture.** For any $s\geq 1$, the simple $I_s$-free and triangle-free binary matroids have bounded critical number.

This conjecture is analogous to the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for graphs. It is trivial for $s=1,2,3$ and was resolved by the authors for $s=4$, but remains open for $s\geq 5$. The analogous assertion fails when triangle-free is replaced by $F_7$-free, because of the even-plane matroids.
original_record.source_name: Peter Nelson and Kazuhiro Nomoto, “The critical number of I_1,t-free triangle-free binary matroids”, arXiv:2011.06625 (2020).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.06625

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

original_record.title: The extremal middle-parts conjecture for binary trees
original_record.statement:
A **binary tree** is a tree in which every vertex has degree $1$ or $3$. A **rooted binary tree** is a rooted tree whose root has degree $2$ and whose other vertices have degree $1$ or $3$. A **rgood binary tree** is a rooted greedy binary tree with root degree $2$ and degree sequence consisting of vertices of degrees $3$, $2$, and $1$. A **binary caterpillar** consists of a path with pendant vertices such that every internal vertex has degree $3$. For a tree $T$, let $C(T)$, $CT(T)$, and $Core(T)$ denote its middle parts, and let $d(A,B)$ denote the distance between middle parts $A$ and $B$. The **eccentricity** of a vertex is its maximum distance from any vertex.

**Extremal middle-parts conjecture.** Among binary trees of order $n$, the tree $T$ that maximizes $d(CT(T), C(T))$ is formed by identifying the root of an rgood binary tree with a vertex of maximum eccentricity in a binary caterpillar. The same tree structure maximizes $d(Core(T), CT(T))$ as well as $d(Core(T), C(T))$.

The conjecture proposes a common extremal structure for three distances between different middle parts of a binary tree. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
original_record.source_name: Heather Smith, László Székely, Hua Wang and Shuai Yuan, “On different "middle parts" of a tree”, arXiv:1701.05215 (2017).
original_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05215

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

original_record.title: Gyárfás' staircase conjecture for binary matrices
original_record.statement:
Let $M$ be an $n\times n$ matrix whose entries are $0$ or $1$. A **homogeneous staircase** is a sequence of entries of one common value, with each successive entry either to the right in the same row or below in the same column; its size is its number of entries.

**Gyárfás' conjecture.** Every $0$-$1$ matrix $M$ of size $n\times n$ contains a homogeneous staircase of size at least $n-1$, equivalently, if $st(M)$ is the maximum size of a homogeneous staircase in $M$ and

$$
st(n)=\min\{st(M):M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n},\}
$$

original_record.title: The maximum-weight cell-zeta conjecture for two-dimensional periods
original_record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a two-dimensional completed primitive graph with $V$ vertices, and let $P^{(0)}_{\mathrm{max}}(\Gamma)$ denote the maximum-weight component of its period. Let $P_-(\Gamma)$ and $P_=(\Gamma)$ be respectively the holomorphic and antiholomorphic cell zeta values, with either value defined to be zero when the corresponding Hamiltonian cycle does not exist. Let ${\mathcal H}_{>0}^2$ denote the space of products of positive-weight multiple zeta values.

**Maximum-weight cell-zeta conjecture.**

$$
P^{(0)}_{\mathrm{max}}(\Gamma)\equiv P_-(\Gamma)+P_=(\Gamma)\mod {\mathcal H}_{>0}^2.
$$

The conjecture identifies the highest-weight part of a two-dimensional completed primitive period modulo products. It is motivated in the source by iterating the preceding lemma and is the precise cell-zeta formulation underlying the earlier forward reference.

original_record.title: The bounded-side conjecture for cells in $BC(2,n)$
original_record.statement: Let $BC(2,n)$ be the stained-glass graph obtained from a $2\times n$ rectangle by the construction described in the paper, and call the bounded regions of this graph **cells**. **Bounded-side conjecture.** The cells in $BC(2,n)$ have at most eight sides, and for $n\geq 19$ they have at most six sides. The claim is motivated by the fact that the analogous cells in $BC(1,n)$ are always triangles or quadrilaterals, but it remains unproved according to the supplied text.
original_record.source_name: Lars Blomberg, Scott R. Shannon and N. J. A. Sloane, “Graphical Enumeration and Stained Glass Windows, 1: Rectangular Grids”, arXiv:2009.07918 (2020).
